exposure: Introduction of Early Essential Newborn Care (EENC)
outcome: Proportion of babies receiving thorough drying
Immediate skin-to-skin contact (SSC) for less than 1 min
Uninterrupted SSC for at least 60 min
Uninterrupted SSC for at least 90 min
cohort: The study included post-partum mothers who had delivered vaginally in the previous 2-24 hours and their newborns, along with observations of randomly selected vaginal deliveries in four public maternity hospitals in Gaza.
finding: The introduction of Early Essential Newborn Care (EENC) significantly improved clinical practices during delivery and in the early post-partum period, including thorough drying, skin-to-skin contact, early breastfeeding, and exclusive breastfeeding before discharge.
mod_finding: All observed improvements in care practices were specifically related to and measured among mothers who had vaginal births.
followup_time: Maternal interviews were conducted 2-24 hours after birth, with some breastfeeding outcomes measured up to the point of hospital discharge (typically 24-48 hours after a vaginal birth).
cross-section timing: Baseline (March and June, 2017), early implementation (January and April, 2018), and full implementation (September, 2018, and June, 2019).
